endpoint: Birth-certificate gestational hypertension versus medical-record abstraction

definitions.TP: certificate yes and medical record yes
definitions.FN: certificate no and medical record yes
definitions.FP: certificate yes and medical record no
definitions.TN: certificate no and medical record no

samples.sampling: 150 births at each of four selected hospitals; PRAMS-based frame with low-birthweight oversampling
samples.precision_note: Raw validation counts are not a nationally representative simple random sample.

samples.sampling: First 125 births per hospital, four selected hospitals; five frame errors excluded
samples.precision_note: Sensitivity has only five true positives. FDR is suppressed in the original because certificate-positive denominator is less than20; derived FDR must not be presented as an officially reported estimate.

samples.sampling: 15 random births per hospital-month across five purposively selected hospitals
samples.precision_note: Publication2019 describes births2013. Item-specific complete-case denominator is892, not900.

transportability_limits: No age-by-smoking-specific outcome error matrices are supplied.
Do not pool these raw counts as one precise national prior; hospital sampling and eras differ.
Medical-record abstraction is an imperfect reference, not verified biological truth.
No direct transport to fetal-death certificates or to2016-2024 without explicit uncertainty/scenarios.
No prior distributions, age/source effects or dependence parameters are locked by this file.
FDR is1-PPV, not1-specificity. Specificity requires the reference-negative denominator.
